texto_en: The European indicator of risk of poverty or social exclusion brings together different dimensions. Secondary data —risk of poverty, material deprivation and low work intensity— help explain the overall picture, but they overlap and should not be added together.
Always cite the age —16 years or over— and distinguish risk of poverty/exclusion from its components. Do not add the secondary indicators together.
Poverty and exclusion indicators overlap; they should not be added together.

In the EU, perceived discrimination among persons with disabilities was more frequent in every area analysed by Eurostat in 2024, from public services to housing and educational institutions.
Persons with and without disabilities; these are not complaints or court decisions

Eurostat asks about perceived discrimination in specific areas. The comparison makes it possible to observe differences in experience between persons with and without disabilities, but it does not replace statistics on complaints or court decisions.
These are percentages of perceived discrimination in specific areas. They are not equivalent to judgments, complaints or legally established discrimination.
The figure must remain linked to its population, territory, year and method. Separating it from that context can change its meaning.

In 2022, CDC’s ADDM Network identified autism in 32.2 per 1,000 8-year-old children —approximately 1 in 31— in 16 U.S. communities. It is one of the most cited autism data points and also one of the most often taken out of context.
Official United States statistics or surveillance
When a new ADDM round is published
8-year-old children in specific communities, not a national survey of all ages
In 2022, CDC’s ADDM Network identified autism in 32.2 per 1,000 8-year-old children in 16 U.S. communities.
CDC states that differences in assessment and identification probably explain part of this variation.

ADDM is a records-based surveillance network. It looks for evidence of autism in health and education records for children of a specific age and in specific communities; it is not a national survey of all ages.
It must appear in full: 8-year-old children, 2022 surveillance, 16 ADDM communities and 32.2 per 1,000. Do not write ‘1 in 31 people in the U.S.’.
‘1 in 31 people in the United States is autistic’.
